title: DDoD
summary: DDoD is a solo and co-op action-shooter RPG with gunplay that feels right and charming mutants you’ll love, or hate. Explore a massive open world above and underground. Don’t get charmed; get to work and cleanse the Purple Lands!
about:
DDoD is a solo and co-op Action-shooter RPG with gunplay that feels right and mutants you’ll love, or hate. Inspired by Diablo-like style and pacing, along with a Stalker-ish vibe and atmosphere.

You arrive at the edge of the Purple Lands — a sealed-off experimental industrial region struck by a sentient substance known as the Fog. Dangerous yet adorable creatures inhabit the territory. Don’t get charmed; they will eat you alive if you get distracted! 

Get to work and cleanse the Purple Lands.

Your journey leads to the very heart of the huge industrial wasteland where experiments took place. Across swamps, forests, and dead villages — to the Source. You’ll scavenge along the way while exploring the open world and dungeons, customize your weapons, and push your luck. It’s up to you to choose the path: the world is huge, and every faction has its own agenda.

ENTER THE PURPLE LANDS

Explore the Purple Lands, once a thriving industrial hub, now a wound in the countryside. The zone is littered with towns, factories, military checkpoints, research bunkers, and various dungeons. It’s 60 km² big and built using real-world topography; the terrain shifts between dense forests, swamps, and industrial ruins. Expect dynamic weather, a full day/night cycle, and warped climates where the landscape itself has been altered by an anomaly.

SURVIVE THE FOG AND ADORABLES

The purple Fog seeps up from the depths of the Purple Lands. Its pockets are dangerous and must be cleansed. Some, like Cryo/Pyro/Electro, shelter a mini-boss and reward the brave. The Fog can jam your weapons without warning, forcing brutal melee encounters. The inhabitants of the Purple Lands have mutated into adorable, visually distinctive, almost endearing, yet lethal creatures. Noise-reactive, each of them has its own way to end your life.

GET TO THE SOURCE. ALONE OR TOGETHER

Every run starts at the base. From there, the route is yours to choose: take side quests to stockpile gear, upgrade your loadout, and explore points of interest. Or gamble everything on a straight shot into the Fog. Run solo, or in 1–4 player co-op to share the loot, revive each other, and ambush the dungeons together. Friends are optional, but recommended.

FAST, LOUD, AND FLUENT GUNPLAY

Tight, responsive top-down shooting with carefully tailored animations and sound effects. Weapon customization and elemental mods that change how each gun behaves in action. Enemies react to noise and player tactics. A pack of mutant hounds and an elite squad of infected mercenaries are two very different things. Fights demand good positioning and tactics.

OTHER KEY FEATURES

• 
Solo or Co-Op. 1–4 player co-op. Face the Purple Lands alone or with up to three friends. Share loot, revive allies, coordinate ambushes, and argue over who’s got to go into the Fog when the batteries fail.
• 
Roguelite Progression. DDoD features a variety of loadouts, points of interest, and weapon modifications. Key upgrades stay, but you’ll have to search for new gear or loot off your body if you die.
• 
Points of Interest. Discover military outposts, secret labs, underground tunnels, and the Fog.
• 
Weapon Customization. Customize your loadout with scopes, silencers, elemental damage mods — fire, cold, electric — and other fog-powered attachments. The right build is crucial.
• 
Battery Management. Your Protection device is a portable safe zone that dispels the Fog when turned on.
• 
A Cast of Crazy Locals. The bunkers of the Purple Lands are home to a roster of fully voiced, eccentric survivors.
